evals.prompt: Something feels off with our Google traffic lately but I can't tell what. Can you dig into it?
evals.expected_output: Should treat this as an open question with no known cause and start with the main report. If the property is unknown, should call seo_sites (or `seo sites`) first. Should run seo_report (or `seo report`) without a section, read the overview against the previous period and the section counts, then pick the one section that fits, such as traffic-drop, or follow the next step the result names. Should not look for a report catalog or call removed tools such as seo_list_reports or seo_run_report. Should name any missing or partial data before interpreting it and should not invent clicks, sessions or rankings.
assertions: Runs seo_report or `seo report` without a section first
Calls seo_sites or `seo sites` when the property is not known
Picks one follow-up section or command from the result instead of running everything
Does not call seo_list_reports, seo_describe_report or seo_run_report
Names missing or partial data before interpreting it
Does not invent clicks, sessions or ranking numbers

evals.prompt: No MCP tools are connected in this session. Get me the main SEO report for example.com as JSON.
evals.expected_output: Should use the CLI. Should check `command -v seo` first, and if it is missing, install it with `npm i -g seo` and tell the person to run `seo start` to sign in with Google. Should then run `seo report --site example.com --json`, and run `seo sites` first if the site is unknown. Should note that JSON mode never prompts. Should read the result before summarizing and should not fabricate output if sign-in is missing.
assertions: Checks whether the seo command is installed before the first call
Uses `npm i -g seo` and `seo start` when the command or sign-in is missing
Runs `seo report` with --json and --site
Does not fabricate report output when the command cannot run

evals.prompt: Run seo quick-wins for example.com like you did last month.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize quick-wins as an old 0.2 command name. Should run the new form, `seo report --section quick-wins` (or seo_report with section quick-wins). May mention that the old name still runs in 0.3 and prints its new command, and that it stops working in 0.4.0. Should not refuse the request because the name changed.
assertions: Runs `seo report --section quick-wins` or seo_report with section quick-wins
Does not rely on the old command name as the primary path
Does not refuse the request because the command was renamed

evals.prompt: Go through the SEO report and fix the title tags on every page that needs it. Just do it, no need to check with me.
evals.expected_output: Should run the report, find the pages whose titles need work, and edit those titles without asking again, because the person said to go ahead. Should show the person the rows it acted on, for example in a table with the page, query, position, CTR and the date window. Should not promise more clicks or better rankings from the changes. Should offer a way to check the result later by running the same section over a later complete window.
assertions: Edits the titles without asking for approval again
Shows the relevant rows to the person, for example in a table
Does not promise more clicks or better rankings
Offers to check the change later with the same command over a later window

evals.prompt: Which of my sites can you actually see?
evals.expected_output: Should call seo_sites (or `seo sites`) and list the Search Console properties the Google sign-in can read. Should not guess or invent properties. If none are returned, should explain the person needs to sign in with a Google account that has Search Console access, through `seo start` or the hosted server sign-in.
assertions: Calls seo_sites or `seo sites`
Lists only the properties returned
Explains how to sign in when no properties are returned
